Retrieve Assistant Reply as Structured Data

Source: R/message_retrieval.R
get_reply_data.Rd

Parses the assistant's reply as JSON and returns the corresponding structured data. If the reply is not marked as JSON, attempts to extract and parse JSON content from the text.

Usage

get_reply_data(.llm, .index = NULL)

last_reply_data(.llm)

Arguments

.llm

An LLMMessage object containing the message history, or a list of them.

.index

A positive integer indicating the index of the assistant reply to retrieve. Defaults to NULL, which retrieves the last reply.

Value

The parsed data from the assistant's reply, or NULL if parsing fails. For a list of replies, a tibble with one row per reply.

Details

For convenience, last_reply_data() is provided as a wrapper to retrieve the latest assistant reply's data.

Given a list of replies, as returned by parallel_chat() or fetch_batch(), it returns a tibble with one row per reply, in the same order. See the section on lists below.

A list of replies

The tibble starts with reply_id (the position in the list), reply (the names of the list, only when it has names) and error. The schema fields follow as columns; a field that holds several values becomes a list-column. error is NA when the reply could be read. A request that failed keeps its row, with the message of the failure in error and NA in the fields, so the rows still match your inputs and filter(!is.na(error)) finds what to run again. A schema field called reply_id, reply or error stops the call, because the table already uses those names. A reply that holds an array of objects gives one row per object, all with the same reply_id.

See also

get_reply(), last_reply_data()
